opened_by: seat lane (during Jericho's R5.3 day-1 window — first real-use defect)
severity: HIGH (Rust lane unusable for stack-using programs; C lane unaffected)
status: RESOLVED — fixed by lane 2026-09-22 ~09:1x CDT, commit 2f619963 (see RECEIPT_R53_day1_auipc_jalr_fix.md). Real second defect was NOT label placement: the glyph JALR lowering indexed the pointer table at rs1 alone, dropping the instruction immediate — rustc's `auipc ra,0; jalr -N(ra)` therefore read its OWN auipc entry (packed 0x3) and spun; gcc's imm=0 `jalr ra,0(a5)` masked it. Fix = fold imm into the index + seed build_pointer_table in glyph_cc runner AND round-trip replay + adopted #[naked] _start (sp). Gate green: rust fib(15) HALT a0=610 roundtrip MATCH; 65 transpiler-family tests pass.
symptom: Any Rust program whose codegen uses `auipc ra,0x0` + `jalr off(ra)` (rustc's standard call pattern) or sp-relative sw/lw with locals/recursion FAULTS or infinite-loops on the Glyph machine. C programs through the same transpiler work (gcc emits `jal`/different patterns). Repro: 4 steps for straight-line Rust (6*7=42 PASS), fault at step 9 the moment a stack frame + recursive call appear.

measured_repro.FAIL: C-parallel: gcc C recursive fib(15) -> a0=610 PASS (same transpiler)

evidence.glyph_output_snippet: at the _start call site, 'auipc ra,0x0; jalr -40(ra)' transpiles to: LDI r1 0x6c; LDI r30 0x2000; ADD r30 r1; LDI r29 2; SHR r30 r29; LD r30 r30; CALLR r30 — i.e. the call TARGET is loaded FROM MEMORY (LD r30 r30) after a shift, instead of being computed register-immediate. Prologue 'sw ra,12(sp)' similarly becomes SHR+ST chains.
evidence.suspicion: byte_to_word_mem addressing: addresses are being materialized then shifted (SHR by 2) and routed through LD/ST even for immediate/register operations; the LD path reads the wrong word address, yielding a garbage CALLR target. gcc codegen (jal with direct targets, different sp addressing) avoids the broken pattern.
evidence.artifact_saved: /tmp/rust_own_start_rec.rs and /tmp/dbg4/ transpile dump (regenerate via glyph_cc; tmp is volatile — ticket text above is the durable record)

r53_context: Opened on day 1 of the 30-day use test. The C lane (glyph_cc program.c) is unaffected and remains usable for real work; the Rust lane is ticketed. This is the use-test working as designed: real use surfaced what the rung gates didn't.
root_cause_CONFIRMED: glyph_cc.py's transpile_and_run/_exec_artifact path never calls build_pointer_table() — the JALR translation emits LDI r30 TBL_BASE; ADD r30 rs1; SHR r30 r29; LD r30 r30; CALLR r30 (rv64i_to_glyph.py:1239-1255) which reads the pointer table from memory, but glyph_cc never seeds that memory. The LD returns unseeded (zero) word -> CALLR to glyph PC 0 -> the observed fault/loop at step 9. Reference implementations output/go5_shell.py:25 and go5_probe4.py:26 DO seed the table via build_pointer_table(...) before running; the R2.3 runner path omitted that step.
why_C_lane_worked: NOT luck, and NOT pattern-dependent: the C lane worked through the same unseeded-table JALR path only for tests whose calls the runner resolved differently. Measured 2026-09-22: C fn-pointer indirect call (jalr ra,0(a5) idiom) PASSES (a0=42), C recursion passes (a0=610) — these run through GlyphCPUv2 with a different entry path that seeds the table. Rust linkage (_RUST_WRAP appended _start section placement) hits the unseeded path. Precise split of which entry path seeds vs not is the lane's first task — the asymmetry is measured but not yet fully attributed.
also_filed_note: Second independent defect (small): _RUST_WRAP (glyph_cc.py:75) never initializes sp — C crt0 does 'li sp,0x4000', the Rust wrapper does not. Any Rust program needing stack fails even with the table seeded. Fix both in one commit + one receipt.

probing_result_20260922.table_seeding_probe: Seeding the pointer table manually (build_pointer_table(text_bytes, text_vaddr, assemble_meta) -> 32 entries -> memory[0x800+wi] = packed) did NOT fix the repro: still faulted at step 9. The LD DID read the correct packed PC (memory[0x81b]=0x10029 = meta(':pc_0000006c')=(41,1) packed). So unseeded-table is REAL (glyph_cc never seeds) but seeded alone is INSUFFICIENT — a second fault follows the call into fib's prologue: POP r30 faults at instruction col 39, apparently mid-BLT-sequence (entry :_start=(col 32,row 1) lands at the CMP of a pushed-compare sequence, POP on unbalanced stack).
probing_result_20260922.coordinates: Coordinate systems verified consistent: meta coords are instruction columns (stride 1 per glyph instr), executor pc is pixel coords (4 px per instr, pixels shape 32x256x3). JMP :_start -> pixel 128 = col 32. No displacement bug.
probing_result_20260922.implication_for_lane: The fix is TWO parts, not one: (1) seed the pointer table in glyph_cc's runner path (necessary), (2) diagnose the post-call fault: _start entry appears to land inside a BLT PUSH/CMP/POP sequence suggesting the label->instruction-column mapping or the listing-vs-assembler alignment is off for multi-line-expanded handlers (BLT expands to 13 glyph instrs). Check assemble_glyph_to_pixels' label placement for labels that follow expanded instruction sequences.
probing_result_20260922.honest_status: necessary condition found and measured; sufficient fix NOT found by seat lane — handed to lane with the gate below
